svg.title: Locate, record and report without leaving the safe reference point
svg.desc: A stationary Victorian emergency location card. First stop at a safe reference point, keep the group together and record the time. With a phone or GNSS display, copy every displayed character, name the app or device and format, add datum, MGA zone and accuracy only if shown or known, and compare a repeated reading with the map and ground. With a paper map, record its title or sheet and date, and mark a possible position only when several map and ground features agree. Without a map or device position, record the last place and time known with confidence, the route already taken, visible features, hazards and group condition, marking uncertainty honestly. Read from one written report and ask the responder to read back important details. If any source disagrees or a field is unknown, write position uncertain and do not guess, round, swap or convert information. The card gives no route recommendation, route to follow, bearing, movement instruction, coordinate example or accuracy guarantee. Its subjective wording-confidence estimates are 90 percent for the core sequence and 70 percent for completeness.
svg.text: Locate, record and report — stay put
WARNING — THIS CARD DOES NOT PROVE A POSITION
Use it while stationary at the safe reference point.
If sources disagree or a detail is unknown: POSITION UNCERTAIN.
Subjective wording-confidence estimate: 90% for the core sequence;
70% for completeness before specialist and reader review.
These rate wording—not position accuracy, contact, rescue or travel safety.
No route to follow, bearing, conversion or movement instruction is given.
Immediate danger and responder directions are controlled by Chapter 4.
1 MAKE ONE SAFE REFERENCE POINT
• Stop. Keep the group together.
• Record the date and time before checking the position.
• Record the last place and time known with confidence.
• Keep this written record with the communication device.
Do not leave a safe reported point merely to improve a reading.
Choose the column below that matches what you actually have.
2A WITH EQUIPMENT
PHONE OR GNSS DISPLAY
• Copy displayed characters exactly.
• Write app/device and position
format only if shown or known.
• Add displayed datum, MGA zone
and accuracy only when shown.
• Repeat without leaving the point.
• Check repeat with map and ground.
PAPER MAP
• Record map title or sheet and date.
• Mark a point only when several
map and ground features agree.
• A map does not prove a track,
crossing or access is open or safe.
Unknown means write “unknown”.
2B WITHOUT EQUIPMENT
NO MAP OR DEVICE POSITION
• Write the last place and time
known with confidence.
• Write the route already taken
since that certain point.
• List visible signs, track names,
structures and terrain features.
• Record current hazards, injuries
and the condition of the group.
• Mark every uncertain detail as
an estimate or “unknown”.
Do not use moss, sun, drainage,
animal paths or guesswork as a
direction command.
Describe honestly; do not invent.
3 MAKE ONE WRITTEN LOCATION REPORT
Include what is available:
• current time and displayed position details;
• app, device and format; datum, zone and accuracy if known;
• last certain place and time, and the route already taken;
• landmarks, hazards, people and urgent medical needs; and
• every field that is an estimate, uncertain or unknown.
Never round, swap, guess or mentally convert the information.
4 REPORT, READ BACK AND KEEP THE RECORD
• Read from the written record slowly.
• Say which details are estimates, uncertain or unknown.
• Ask the responder to read back important location details.
• Write down direct instructions and any communication status.
Use Chapter 3 for 000, satellite SOS, PLB and message status.
IF INFORMATION DISAGREES: STOP
Write POSITION UNCERTAIN. Do not force the sources to match.
Do not choose a route from this card or wander to test a guess.
Stay at the safe reference point unless it becomes immediately
dangerous or a responsible responder directs otherwise.
WORKING DRAFT — SAR, geospatial and reader review outstanding
